instruction:
GUI-only requirement: Complete the task entirely in the launched Revit graphical user interface. Do not open Command Prompt, PowerShell, Terminal, Dynamo, pyRevit, macros, external API automation, Python, or any helper script/code that directly generates or edits the deliverable files. Use only Revit native GUI tools, menus, dialogs, schedules, sheets, and built-in export commands. Start from a blank Revit project. Using the Revit GUI, create a single-storey loading hall building with an overall rectangular footprint of 24.0 m by 14.0 m near the project origin. The exterior walls should rise about 5.0 m, with one ground slab and a roof covering the footprint. Add a real structural grid of columns and beams: columns should span the hall height and beams should sit near the roof level. Save the deliverables on the Desktop using the exact filenames required below.

The IFC export must use the IFC4 schema, have unique GlobalId values for all IfcRoot objects, and contain one IfcProject, one IfcSite, one IfcBuilding, one IfcBuildingStorey, three IfcSpace entities, four IfcWall entities, one IfcSlab, one IfcRoof, three IfcDoor entities, twelve IfcColumn entities, and seventeen IfcBeam entities. Do not include IfcWindow, IfcStair, IfcCurtainWall, or IfcBuildingElementProxy entities. Name the spaces so the normalized IfcSpace names include Office, Service, and Hall. Export a Revit structural count schedule named result.csv with headers category,count and exactly two rows, Columns=12 and Beams=17; the schedule counts must match the IFC column and beam counts. The required BIM categories must be exported as real IFC building elements/spaces, not visual-only placeholders or proxy geometry. Coordinate placement, relationship entities, GUID values, Revit type names, materials, property sets, and harmless extra metadata may vary as long as the stated model geometry, element categories, space names, schedules, sheets, and file outputs are satisfied.
